p1_b1.ocr: Hepatol Int (2016) 10:158–168 Statistical analysis Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted to identify the potential predictors of SVR24 and viral relapse. Univariate analyses were sequentially performed for each independent variable to identify potential factors for further multivariate analysis. Fisher’s exact test and logistic regression models were used for comparisons between individual categorical independent variables and continuous variables, respectively. Variables with p values of \0.10 in the univariate analyses were included in the multivariate logistic regression analysis, which was per- formed using stepwise (backward) regression, and ana- lyzed again for statistical signiﬁcance. A p value of \0.05 was considered signiﬁcant. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were con- structed for each logistic model, and the areas under the ROC (AUROC) curves were evaluated for predictive performance analysis. The 95 % conﬁdence interval (CI) of the AUROC was computed by resampling 10,000 times (bootstrapping). The sensitivity and speciﬁcity of the ROC curves were determined at the cutoff point where (sensitivity ? speci- ﬁcity - 1) it was maximal in the ROC curve (Youden index). ROC analysis was performed using the full model (including all statistically signiﬁcant independent variables) as well as the limited model (each independent variable).
